findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on file-not-found or I/O error
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> and propagate with ? instead of unwrap()

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric or missing second field
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV lines abort the program instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to extract fields, chain .map_err() on parse to return a domain error, and handle missing second field

findings.problem: Lossy cast from u32 to u16 via `as u16` silently truncates values >= 65536
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value in the range 65536-18446744073709551615 wraps to an incorrect u16 instead of being rejected
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) and map_err to return a typed overflow error

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses the Vec without bounds checking; a line with no commas yields an empty parts Vec
findings.failure_mode: Index out of bounds panic on blank or comma-less lines
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') which yields an Option<( &str, &str )> and handle the None case

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses the Vec without bounds checking; a line with only one comma field yields a single-element parts Vec
findings.failure_mode: Index out of bounds panic on lines missing the value field
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and destructure the second part from the returned tuple

findings.problem: println!() is a side effect inside the parsing/transform pipeline; I/O is embedded in the core
findings.failure_mode: Pure pipeline is no longer deterministic or testable without suppressing stdout; logging leaks into the data layer
findings.fix: Remove println! from the mapping closure. If logging is needed, push it to the shell layer after parsing completes, or pass a callback mechanism

findings.problem: Uses split(',') + collect() into Vec<String> when split_once(',') suffices for a two-field record
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary allocation of Vec<String> for every line, plus O(n) split over all commas when only the first matters
findings.fix: Replace with line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::MissingDelimiter) to extract name and value parts in O(1) per line

findings.problem: Record uses String instead of a newtyped domain value for name
findings.failure_mode: No compile-time guarantee that name is non-empty or valid; callers can construct Record with empty or malformed names
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype Name(String) with a fallible constructor that rejects empty names, use it in Record

findings.problem: load_quotes returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failures are silenced via unwrap
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot distinguish I/O errors, parse errors, or overflow errors; all manifest as panics
findings.fix: Define a domain error enum (e.g. LoadError::Io, LoadError::Parse, LoadError::Overflow) and return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: Allocates Vec<String> for every line via .map().collect() before accessing two fields
findings.failure_mode: Excess heap allocations per line; each line allocates a Vec<String> plus two owned Strings
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to borrow &str slices from the line; only allocate String for the final Record fields

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists to measure parse-throughput or allocation profile
no profiler data for load_quotes hot path
no allocation tracing (e.g. dhat, afl, or built-in allocator hooks) for the per-line allocation pattern
no second-ring testing (Miri, Kani, or proptest) for edge cases on malformed CSV lines
no command-level evidence that load_quotes handles the full spectrum of I/O and parse failure modes
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has 7 BLOCKER violations (unwrap on I/O and parse, lossy as cast, two unchecked indexings, side effect in core, over-allocation pattern) and 3 MAJOR violations (no domain newtypes, no error enum, excess allocation). All unwrap and unchecked-index paths are panic vectors on untrusted input. The code must be refactored to use split_once, Result propagation, try_from for the u16 cast, and remove println! before any delivery.
